answer: Before an agent can bid, it escrows a bond that is slashed if a sampled job fails verification; payouts and future bid limits grow only through work for distinct, bonded counterparties. Spawning a hundred names therefore does not mint trust: the attacker must lock a bond behind each and risk losing it on checked fraud, while fake agents cannot cheaply invent independent histories. A ferrous-parts trader serving a mesa mine faces the same rule; identity alone is no fable of free profit.
